claim: ESCRT-III polymerization is required for all ESCRT-dependent events in the cell.
source: ESCRT-III polymerization is required for all endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT)-dependent events in the cell.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a general principle about ESCRT-III function.

claim: The relative contributions of the eight ESCRT-III subunits differ between each process.
source: However, the relative contributions of the eight ESCRT-III subunits differ between each process.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript showing differential requirements for different ESCRT-III subunits.

claim: The helix-4 region of Snf7 associates with the helix-1 region of Vps24.
source: To identify essential features of ESCRT-III subunits, we previously studied the polymerization mechanisms of two ESCRT-III subunits Snf7 and Vps24, identifying the association of the helix-4 region of Snf7 with the helix-1 region of Vps24 (Banjade et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Mutations in the helix-1 region of Vps2 can functionally replace Vps24 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source: Here, we find that mutations in the helix-1 region of another ESCRT-III subunit Vps2 can functionally replace Vps24 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data including Mup1-pHluorin sorting assays and canavanine sensitivity assays.

claim: Three minimal features are required for ESCRT-III function: spiral formation, lateral association of the spirals through heteropolymerization, and binding to the AAA + ATPase Vps4 for dynamic remodeling.
source: Our data allow us to propose three minimal features required for ESCRT-III function – spiral formation, lateral association of the spirals through heteropolymerization, and binding to the AAA + ATPase Vps4 for dynamic remodeling.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: ESCRT-III is required in all ESCRT-dependent processes.
source: Among the different subcomplexes of ESCRTs, ESCRT-III is required in all processes, while the requirement of the other upstream complexes 0, I, and II is variable (Henne et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The requirement of ESCRT complexes 0, I, and II is variable across different ESCRT-dependent processes.
source: Among the different subcomplexes of ESCRTs, ESCRT-III is required in all processes, while the requirement of the other upstream complexes 0, I, and II is variable (Henne et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Eight ESCRT-III proteins exist in eukaryotes: Did2 (CHMP1), Vps2 (CHMP2), Vps24 (CHMP3), Snf7 (CHMP4), Vps60 (CHMP5), Vps20 (CHMP6), Chm7 (CHMP7), and Ist1 (IST1).
source: In eukaryotes, eight ESCRT-III proteins exist: Did2 (CHMP1), Vps2 (CHMP2), Vps24 (CHMP3), Snf7 (CHMP4), Vps60 (CHMP5), Vps20 (CHMP6), Chm7 (CHMP7), and Ist1 (IST1) (Rue et al., 2008; McCullough et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Vps20, Snf7, Vps24, and Vps2 are individually essential for multivesicular body (MVB) biogenesis in yeast.
source: Of these, Vps20, Snf7, Vps24, and Vps2 have been studied in greater detail, because they are individually essential for multivesicular body (MVB) biogenesis in yeast, the earliest ascribed role for ESCRTs.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about these proteins.

claim: Vps20, Snf7, Vps24, and Vps2 are the minimal subunits necessary to create intraluminal vesicles in the MVB pathway.
source: These four proteins are the minimal subunits necessary to create intraluminal vesicles in the MVB pathway, as suggested by in vivo and in vitro analyses (Adell et al., 2017; Schöneberg et al., 2018; Pfitzner et al., 2020; Teis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Vps24 and Vps2 are essential for MVB biogenesis.
source: Vps24 and Vps2 are essential for MVB biogenesis (Henne et al., 2012; Babst et al., 2002; Buchkovich et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Vps24 and Vps2 are recruited cooperatively to membranes, requiring each one for the other's efficient recruitment.
source: Vps24 and Vps2 are also recruited cooperatively to membranes, requiring each one for the other's efficient recruitment (Adell et al., 2017; Mierzwa et al., 2017; Babst et al., 2002; Banjade et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: During HIV budding, CHMP2 (the human ortholog of Vps2) is essential, but CHMP3 (the human Vps24 ortholog) is not essential for HIV egress from cells.
source: Interestingly, in previous work, it was found that during HIV budding, while CHMP2 (the human ortholog of Vps2) is essential, CHMP3 (the human Vps24 ortholog) is not essential for HIV egress from cells (Morita et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Vps2 recruits the AAA + ATPase Vps4, which modifies ESCRT-III polymers.
source: One of the most important features of Vps2 that has previously been described is the recruitment of the AAA + ATPase Vps4, which modifies ESCRT-III polymers (Obita et al., 2007; Adell et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Vps24 and Vps2 bind to Snf7 and remodel Snf7 polymerization, changing the flat Snf7 spiral into three-dimensional (3D) helices.
source: Vps24 and Vps2 bind to Snf7 and remodel Snf7 polymerization, changing the flat Snf7 spiral into three-dimensional (3D) helices (Henne et al., 2012; Moser von Filseck et al., 2020; Pfitzner et al., 2020; Banjade et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Overexpressing VPS24 suppresses the defect of a snf7 allele (snf7-D131K) that encodes a Snf7 mutant with a lower affinity to Vps24.
source: In our previous work (Banjade et al., 2019a), we observed that overexpressing VPS24 suppresses the defect of a snf7 allele (snf7-D131K) that encodes a Snf7 mutant with a lower affinity to Vps24.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Overexpression of Vps2 rescues the defect of snf7-D131K.
source: We also observed that overexpression of Vps2 rescues the defect of snf7-D131K.
evidence: This is stated as a previous observation by the authors.

claim: Vps24 and Vps2 bind synergistically to Snf7.
source: These data are consistent with the observations that Vps24 and Vps2 bind synergistically to Snf7 (Adell et al., 2017; Mierzwa et al., 2017; Babst et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CHMP3 possesses a 16-fold tighter affinity than CHMP2A to mammalian Snf7 (CHMP4A).
source: These ideas are also consistent with previous binding-constant measurements with mammalian Vps2 (CHMP2A) and Vps24 (CHMP3), which showed that CHMP3 possesses a 16-fold tighter affinity than CHMP2A to mammalian Snf7 (CHMP4A) (Effantin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: VPS2 overexpression rescues the temperature sensitivity of vps24∆.
source: We also noted that VPS2 overexpression rescues the temperature sensitivity of vps24∆ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that the increased concentration of Vps2 could replace the cellular function of Vps24 beyond MVB cargo sorting.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: About eightfold overexpression of Vps2 is necessary for restoring Mup1 sorting in vps24∆.
source: As a result, we determined that about eightfold overexpression of Vps2 is necessary for restoring Mup1 sorting (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: Vps2 contains features that can replace the function of Vps24 when present in higher concentrations in cells.
source: These data suggested that Vps2 contains features that can replace the function of Vps24 when present in higher concentrations in cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that overexpression of Vps2 can rescue vps24∆.

claim: Vps2RM contains mutations in its promoter region, three missense mutations in helix 1 (N21K T28A E31K), and two missense mutations in helix 4 (S136N M146I).
source: Vps2RM contains mutations in its promoter region, three missense mutations in helix 1 (N21K T28A E31K), and two missense mutations in helix 4 (S136N M146I).
evidence: This is a description of the mutations identified in the Vps2RM allele from the random mutagenesis screen.

claim: The N-terminal mutations E21K T28A N31K are necessary and sufficient for the suppression effect of Vps2RM.
source: The N-terminal mutations E21K T28A N31K (with the promoter mutations, hereafter called Vps2*, Figure 1C schematic) are necessary and sufficient for the suppression effect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that these mutations alone can rescue vps24∆.

claim: The mutations in Vps2* lie on the same surface of the alpha-1 helix.
source: Interestingly, these mutants also lie on the same surface of the alpha-1 helix, as a helical wheel representation suggests (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The expression level of Vps2* is increased about threefold.
source: Because the mutant we isolated also had promoter mutations, the expression level of Vps2* is increased about threefold (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The suppression by Vps2* is not due simply to the overexpression effect.
source: The suppression by Vps2* is not due simply to the overexpression effect however, since about eightfold overexpression of Vps2 is required for only ~20% sorting of Mup1 to occur in a vps24∆ strain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of experimental data showing that Vps2* at threefold overexpression is more effective than wild-type Vps2 at eightfold overexpression.

claim: vps2* suppresses vps24∆vps2∆.
source: We observed that vps2* also suppresses vps24∆vps2∆ (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A–B.

claim: A synergistic effect of the mutations in the N-terminal basic region of Vps2 helix 1 and its threefold overexpression provides the necessary functional features of Vps24 and Vps2.
source: Therefore, a synergistic effect of the mutations in the N-terminal basic region of Vps2 helix 1 and its threefold overexpression provides the necessary functional features of Vps24 and Vps2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that vps2* can replace both Vps24 and Vps2.

claim: In the absence of Vps24, Vps2 does not bind to Snf7.
source: In the absence of Vps24, Vps2 does not bind to Snf7 (Teis et al., 2008; Babst et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Vps2* binds to Snf7 at a lower expression level than the WT Vps2.
source: In co-immunoprecipation experiments, Vps2* binds to Snf7 at a lower expression level than the WT Vps2, suggesting that the N-terminal helix-1 mutations increase the affinity of Vps2 for Snf7, bypassing the need for Vps24 (Figure 2C-D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: The N-terminal helix-1 mutations increase the affinity of Vps2 for Snf7, bypassing the need for Vps24.
source: In co-immunoprecipation experiments, Vps2* binds to Snf7 at a lower expression level than the WT Vps2, suggesting that the N-terminal helix-1 mutations increase the affinity of Vps2 for Snf7, bypassing the need for Vps24 (Figure 2C-D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: The overall features of helix-1 region of Vps24 and Vps2 are similar (both basic helices), but they vary in sequence composition.
source: Although the overall features of helix-1 region of Vps24 and Vps2 are similar (both basic helices), they vary in sequence composition (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The charge inversions in Vps2* increase the affinity of the basic patch of Vps2* to Snf7's acidic helix 4.
source: Since the mutations occur in polar residues (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–B), it is possible that these charge inversions increase the affinity of the basic patch of Vps2* to Snf7's acidic helix 4, consistent with our observations of Vps24 binding to Snf7 through an electrostatic interface (Banjade et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the location of the mutations and previous observations about Vps24-Snf7 interactions.

claim: Simple overexpression of Vps2 rescues the defect of the lack of Vps24 because the overall concentration of a lower affinity Snf7 binding Vps2 molecule is increased in the cytoplasm.
source: Simple overexpression of Vps2 probably rescues the defect of the lack of Vps24 since the overall concentration of a lower affinity Snf7 binding Vps2 molecule is increased in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that high levels of Vps2 can rescue vps24∆.

claim: Defects resulting from charge inversion mutations in helix-4 region of Snf7 are rescued by helix-1 charge-inversion mutations in Vps2.
source: Consistent with the model of helix-1 region of Vps24 and Vps2 interacting with helix-4 region of Snf7, Teis and colleagues report that defects resulting from charge inversion mutations in helix-4 region of Snf7 are rescued by helix-1 charge-inversion mutations in Vps2 (Sprenger et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to work by Teis and colleagues.

claim: Vps2 associates with Snf7 in a lateral assembly mechanism, similar to Vps24.
source: Collectively, these results provide strong evidence of the similarity between Vps24 and Vps2, supporting the idea that Vps2 associates with Snf7 in a lateral assembly mechanism, similar to Vps24.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and cited work.

claim: Vps24 overexpression by ~16-fold did not rescue the defect of a vps2∆.
source: In contrast to Vps2 overexpression rescuing the defects of vps24∆, the reverse does not occur – Vps24 overexpression by ~16-fold did not rescue the defect of a vps2∆ (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The Vps2 MIM has the strongest affinity for Vps4 in solution (~20 µM).
source: While other ESCRT-III proteins also possess the MIM motifs, the Vps2 MIM has the strongest affinity for Vps4 in solution (~20 µM, Obita et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Helix 5 of Vps2 has been identified as a second binding site of Vps4 with an affinity of ~3 µM.
source: In addition, helix 5 of Vps2 has been identified as a second binding site of Vps4 with an affinity of ~3 µM (Han et al., 2015; Han et al., 2017; Han et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Replacing the C-terminus of Vps24 with that of Vps2 keeps the protein functional in vps24∆.
source: Consistent with the sequence analysis, replacing the MIM and helix 5 of Vps24 with the homologous region of Vps2 kept the protein functional, but truncations beyond residue ~152 resulted in functional defects.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Chimeras with the N-terminus of Vps24 and helix 5 and MIM of Vps2 do not functionally restore the loss of Vps2 under endogenous promoters.
source: We next tested these chimeras in vps2∆. In contrast to vps24∆ cells, we observed that they do not functionally restore the loss of Vps2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Overexpressed chimeras with the N-terminus of Vps24 and helix 5 and MIM of Vps2 modestly suppress the defect of vps2∆ to about 30% of WT.
source: We found that they modestly suppress the defect of vps2∆ to about 30% of WT (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Directly recruiting Vps4 on to Vps24 partially bypasses the requirement of Vps2.
source: Therefore, directly recruiting Vps4 on to Vps24 partially bypasses the requirement of Vps2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that Vps24 chimeras with Vps4 binding sites can partially rescue vps2∆.

claim: vps24E114K when overexpressed robustly rescues the defect of vps2∆ when it carries the Vps4 binding motifs of Vps2.
source: As a result, we found that vps24E114K when overexpressed robustly rescues the defect of vps2∆ when it carries the Vps4 binding motifs of Vps2 (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: A Vps24 variant capable of auto-activation and Vps4 recruitment can function as Vps2.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that a Vps24 variant capable of auto-activation and Vps4 recruitment can function as Vps2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that activated Vps24 with Vps4 binding sites can replace Vps2.

claim: Snf7-Vps2 chimeras with helix 5 and MIM of Vps2 were unable to replace either Vps24 or Vps2.
source: However, we found that these chimeras were unable to replace either Vps24 or Vps2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the function of Vps24-Vps2 goes beyond merely being adaptors to recruit the AAA + ATPase.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The function of Vps24-Vps2 goes beyond merely being adaptors to recruit the AAA + ATPase.
source: However, we found that these chimeras were unable to replace either Vps24 or Vps2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the function of Vps24-Vps2 goes beyond merely being adaptors to recruit the AAA + ATPase.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that Snf7 with Vps4 binding sites cannot replace Vps24-Vps2.

claim: Vps24-Vps2 act as laterally interacting proteins to Snf7 polymers that induce 3D helicity.
source: Since previous publications (Adell et al., 2017; Bertin et al., 2020) and we ourselves (Teis et al., 2008) have found that Vps24-Vps2 act as laterally interacting proteins to Snf7 polymers that induce 3D helicity, an ESCRT-III functional protein requires this lateral copolymerization, perhaps to regulate Vps4-mediated subunit turnover of the heteropolymers.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: An ESCRT-III functional protein requires lateral copolymerization, perhaps to regulate Vps4-mediated subunit turnover of the heteropolymers.
source: Since previous publications (Adell et al., 2017; Bertin et al., 2020) and we ourselves (Teis et al., 2008) have found that Vps24-Vps2 act as laterally interacting proteins to Snf7 polymers that induce 3D helicity, an ESCRT-III functional protein requires this lateral copolymerization, perhaps to regulate Vps4-mediated subunit turnover of the heteropolymers.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and cited work.

claim: Vps24E114K in cell lysates forms higher molecular weight species in glycerol-gradient experiments.
source: Consistent with these ideas, Vps24E114K in cell lysates (containing both the membrane and soluble fragments) forms higher molecular weight species in glycerol-gradient experiments (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Vps24E114K readily associates into linear filaments with Vps2 in vitro.
source: In in vitro assays, while the WT Vps24 does not form polymers by itself or with Vps2 (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), Vps24E114K readily associates into linear filaments with Vps2 (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: WT Vps24 does not form polymers by itself or with Vps2 in vitro at low concentrations.
source: In in vitro assays, while the WT Vps24 does not form polymers by itself or with Vps2 (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), Vps24E114K readily associates into linear filaments with Vps2 (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Both WT and the mutant Vps24 are able to form 3D spirals with Snf7 and Vps2.
source: With Snf7 and Vps2, both WT and the mutant Vps24 are able to form 3D spirals, which we previously described as the copolymeric structure of Snf7, Vps24, and Vps2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The E114K mutation shifts the equilibrium of Vps24 to a polymerization-competent state.
source: The increased ability to form polymers is consistent with the interpretation that E114K shifts the equilibrium of Vps24 to a polymerization-competent state.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing increased polymerization of Vps24E114K.

claim: Mutating the Asn to helix-stabilizing Ala in the hinge region of Vps24 (in addition to the Vps4 binding motifs) rescues the defect of vps2∆.
source: We found that mutating the Asn to helix-stabilizing Ala (in addition to the Vps4 binding motifs) in Vps24 rescues the defect of vps2∆, while the helix-breaking glycine does not rescue the defect (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Mutating the Asn to helix-breaking glycine in the hinge region of Vps24 does not rescue the defect of vps2∆.
source: We found that mutating the Asn to helix-stabilizing Ala (in addition to the Vps4 binding motifs) in Vps24 rescues the defect of vps2∆, while the helix-breaking glycine does not rescue the defect (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The hinge region, in addition to the Vps4 binding sites, accounts for the majority of the difference between Vps24 and Vps2.
source: Therefore, it appears that the hinge region, that contains residues which may affect the conformational flexibility of ESCRT-III proteins, in addition to the Vps4 binding sites, accounts for the majority of the difference between Vps24 and Vps2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that mutations in the hinge region affect function.

claim: Overexpressing a variant that replaces the hinge region of Vps2 with that of Vps24 suppresses vps24∆ to ~80% as tested by Mup1 sorting, compared to ~40% for that of the WT Vps2.
source: Consistent with this, when we overexpress a variant that replaces the hinge region of Vps2 with that of Vps24, it suppresses vps24∆ to ~80% as tested by Mup1 sorting, compared to ~40% for that of the WT Vps2 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Vps24 and Vps2 contain similar features: laterally interacting with Snf7, inducing the formation of an ESCRT-III super-helix, and recruiting Vps4.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that Vps24 and Vps2 contain similar features. Laterally interacting with Snf7, inducing the formation of an ESCRT-III super-helix, and recruiting Vps4 are three features for the Vps24-Vps2 module.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: snf7∆, vps20∆, vps24∆, and vps2∆ show severe sorting defects.
source: We observed that snf7∆, vps20∆, vps24∆, and vps2∆ show severe sorting defects, did2∆ and vps60∆ show partial sorting defects, and ist1∆ and chm7∆ show no defect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: did2∆ and vps60∆ show partial sorting defects.
source: We observed that snf7∆, vps20∆, vps24∆, and vps2∆ show severe sorting defects, did2∆ and vps60∆ show partial sorting defects, and ist1∆ and chm7∆ show no defect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: ist1∆ and chm7∆ show no defect in Mup1-pHluorin sorting.
source: We observed that snf7∆, vps20∆, vps24∆, and vps2∆ show severe sorting defects, did2∆ and vps60∆ show partial sorting defects, and ist1∆ and chm7∆ show no defect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Snf7, Vps20, Vps24, and Vps2 are the minimal contributors in MVB formation.
source: These data are consistent with previous findings with a different cargo (CPS) (Rue et al., 2008), and from in vitro assays (Schöneberg et al., 2018; Pfitzner et al., 2020), which suggest that Snf7, Vps20, Vps24, and Vps2 are the minimal contributors in MVB formation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and the experimental data in this study.

claim: Vps2 overexpression partially rescued the defect of a did2∆.
source: As described above, Vps2 overexpression rescued the defect of vps24∆ and also partially rescued the defect of a did2∆ (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Did2 forms tube-like helices in in vitro assays with lipid monolayers.
source: In in vitro assays with lipid monolayers, we found that Did2 forms tube-like helices (Figure 6B, and as previously shown in McCullough et al., 2015; Nguyen et al., 2020 for mammalian Did2 named CHMP1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and citations to previous work.

claim: Vps60 lacks the ability to form long helices/tubes, and preferentially forms spiral-like structures, reminiscent of Snf7.
source: However, Vps60 lacks the ability to form long helices/tubes, and preferentially forms spiral-like structures, reminiscent of Snf7 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The N-terminal region of Snf7 fused to the C-terminal region of Vps60 rescues the defects of vps60∆.
source: Consistent with Vps60 mimicking Snf7 structurally, the N-terminal region of Snf7 fused to the C-terminal region of Vps60 rescues the defects of vps60∆ (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Vps60-GFP is localized to endosomal and vacuolar membranes with a hint of plasma membrane signal.
source: Vps60-GFP is localized to endosomal and vacuolar membranes with a hint of plasma membrane signal (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Vps60-GFP localization is primarily cytosolic in vps20∆, snf7∆, or vps2∆.
source: This localization is primarily cytosolic in vps20∆, snf7∆, or vps2∆, and unchanged in did2∆ (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Among Vps20-Snf7-Vps60, Snf7 serves as the main scaffold which can be engineered to substitute for Vps20 or Vps60.
source: In summary, among Vps20-Snf7-Vps20, Snf7 serves as the main scaffold which can be engineered to substitute for Vps20 (Tang et al., 2016) or Vps60 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in this study and citation to previous work.

claim: Modifications within Vps24-Vps2 can functionally replace each other.
source: Among Vps24-Vps2-Did2, modifications within Vps24-Vps2 can functionally replace each other; Did2 resembles Vps24-Vps2 as it readily forms 3D helices, and did2∆ can be partially suppressed by Vps2 overexpression.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Did2 resembles Vps24-Vps2 as it readily forms 3D helices.
source: Among Vps24-Vps2-Did2, modifications within Vps24-Vps2 can functionally replace each other; Did2 resembles Vps24-Vps2 as it readily forms 3D helices, and did2∆ can be partially suppressed by Vps2 overexpression.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Rational modifications in ESCRT-III subunits can allow one to consolidate the functions of two ESCRT-III proteins into one ESCRT-III protein.
source: Our data suggest that although ESCRT-III subunits have evolved for divergent roles in ordered assembly, rational modifications in ESCRT-III subunits can allow one to consolidate the functions of two ESCRT-III proteins into one ESCRT-III protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Overexpression of Vps2, by approximately eight fold and above, can rescue vps24∆ in yeast.
source: First, we find that overexpression of Vps2, by approximately eight fold and above, can rescue vps24∆ in yeast.
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Point mutations in the helix-1 region of Vps2 can rescue vps24∆.
source: Second, point mutations in the helix-1 region of Vps2 can also rescue vps24∆.
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Vps2 mutants with point mutations in helix-1 bind to Snf7 in vivo even in the absence of Vps24.
source: These Vps2 mutants also bind to Snf7 in vivo even in the absence of Vps24.
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Overexpression and inclusion of higher affinity AAA + ATPase Vps4 binding regions on Vps24 can rescue the absence of Vps2.
source: Third, overexpression and inclusion of higher affinity AAA + ATPase Vps4 binding regions on Vps24 can rescue the absence of Vps2.
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Mutations that 'activate' Vps24-Vps2, by possibly inducing conformational changes, rescue each other's function.
source: Fourth, mutations that 'activate' Vps24-Vps2, by possibly inducing conformational changes, also rescue each other's function.
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Vps24 may not possess the ability to fully extend its helices 2 and 3 in the ESCRT-III copolymer.
source: Our data suggest that Vps24 may not possess the ability to fully extend its helices 2 and 3 in the ESCRT-III copolymer.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and structural analysis.

claim: A recently published CryoEM structure showed that the Vps24 homopolymer consists of Vps24 protomers in a 'semi-open' conformation.
source: A recently published CryoEM structure showed that the Vps24 homopolymer consists of Vps24 protomers in a 'semi-open' conformation (Huber et al., 2020) (see Figure 4—figure supplement 2 for direct comparison), in contrast to the fully extended and open Snf7 (Tang et al., 2015) and Did2 (CHMP1) (Nguyen et al., 2020) polymers.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: A mixture of different conformations allows for efficient Vps24-Vps2 assembly, which has a higher affinity to the Snf7 polymer.
source: It is possible that a mixture of different conformations allows for efficient Vps24-Vps2 assembly, which has a higher affinity to the Snf7 polymer.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the structural and experimental data.

claim: Vps2 consists of a higher affinity Vps4 binding site compared to Vps24.
source: Despite the observed similarity between Vps24 and Vps2, our data also suggest some differences: they may exist in different conformations, and that Vps2 consists of a higher affinity Vps4 binding site, consistent with previous mammalian CHMP2 and CHMP3 work (Effantin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Vps24-Vps2 induce lateral association and bundling, along with helicity of the spirals.
source: In addition, Vps24-Vps2 induce lateral association and bundling (Mierzwa et al., 2017; Pfitzner et al., 2020; Banjade et al., 2019a), along with helicity of the spirals, which could be an important parameter for ESCRT-III function for MVB biogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Heteropolymerization of Vps2 and Vps24 into an elongated polymer, interacting 'longitudinally' with the helices 2 and 3, is consistent with the model presented by Teis and colleagues.
source: Heteropolymerization of Vps2 and Vps24 into an elongated polymer, interacting 'longitudinally' with the helices 2 and 3, is also consistent with the model presented in the manuscript by Teis and colleagues (Sprenger et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to work by Teis and colleagues.

claim: Site-specific cysteine mutations in helices 2 and 3 of Vps24 and Vps2 crosslinked with one another.
source: In their work, the authors show through crosslinking experiments that site-specific cysteine mutations in helices 2 and 3 of Vps24 and Vps2 crosslinked with one another, and charge inversion mutations in helix 2/3 also rescued each other's defects.
evidence: This is supported by citation to work by Teis and colleagues.

claim: Vps24's 'opening' could trigger longitudinal heteropolymerization with Vps2.
source: Therefore, similar to Snf7's 'activating' mutations triggering its longitudinal polymerization through helix 2/3 (3, 8, 29), Vps24's 'opening' could also trigger longitudinal heteropolymerization with Vps2.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental data and cited work.

claim: The three critical aspects of an ESCRT-III minimal module are: (1) a core spiral forming unit (e.g., Snf7), (2) a lateral bundling unit (e.g., Vps24 and Vps2), and (3) an ability to recruit a disassembly machinery (e.g., the AAA + ATPase Vps4).
source: Following these observations, we propose the following three critical aspects of an ESCRT-III minimal module: (1) a core spiral forming unit (e.g., Snf7), (2) a lateral bundling unit (e.g., Vps24 and Vps2), and (3) an ability to recruit a disassembly machinery (e.g., the AAA + ATPase Vps4) (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Snf7, Vps24, and Vps2 are essential for membrane budding in vitro.
source: In vitro reconstitutions suggest that Snf7, Vps24, and Vps2 are essential for membrane budding, and Vps4 for vesicle scission (Schöneberg et al., 2018; Pfitzner et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Vps4 is essential for vesicle scission in vitro.
source: In vitro reconstitutions suggest that Snf7, Vps24, and Vps2 are essential for membrane budding, and Vps4 for vesicle scission (Schöneberg et al., 2018; Pfitzner et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Vps4-mediated turnover of a laterally associating and helix-inducing polymer of Vps24-Vps2 would constrict the Snf7 scaffold to a fission-competent structure.
source: Vps4-mediated turnover of a laterally associating and helix-inducing polymer of Vps24-Vps2 would constrict the Snf7 scaffold to a fission-competent structure, as predicted by simulations (Harker-Kirschneck et al., 2019) and as recently proposed to occur in archaeal cell division (Tarrason Risa et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Did2 and Ist1 are not essential for intraluminal vesicle formation in vitro and in vivo.
source: While Did2 and Ist1 are not essential for intraluminal vesicle formation in vitro and in vivo, they have regulatory roles that are controlled by sequential polymerization dynamics through Vps4 (Pfitzner et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Did2 and Ist1 have regulatory roles that are controlled by sequential polymerization dynamics through Vps4.
source: While Did2 and Ist1 are not essential for intraluminal vesicle formation in vitro and in vivo, they have regulatory roles that are controlled by sequential polymerization dynamics through Vps4 (Pfitzner et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: For Vps60 recruitment to endosomal/vacuole membranes, Vps2 (and likely Vps24) is required.
source: We find that for Vps60 recruitment to endosomal/vacuole membranes, Vps2 (and likely Vps24) is required.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Vps60 may be recruited in later stages of polymer formation, in a sequential fashion to the core scaffold, as Did2 does.
source: Therefore, Vps60 may be recruited in later stages of polymer formation, in a sequential fashion to the core scaffold, as Did2 does (Pfitzner et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and cited work.

claim: Vps60 has been shown to interact with Vta1.
source: Vps60 has been shown to interact with Vta1 (Yang et al., 2012; Azmi et al., 2008; Nickerson et al., 2010), and Vta1 is known to be an activator of Vps4 (Yang et al., 2012; Norgan et al., 2013; Monroe et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Vta1 is known to be an activator of Vps4.
source: Vps60 has been shown to interact with Vta1 (Yang et al., 2012; Azmi et al., 2008; Nickerson et al., 2010), and Vta1 is known to be an activator of Vps4 (Yang et al., 2012; Norgan et al., 2013; Monroe et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Vps60 is possibly involved in further activating Vps4 function in the later stages of polymer dynamics.
source: Therefore, it is possible that Vps60 is involved in further activating Vps4 function in the later stages of polymer dynamics.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the known interactions of Vps60 with Vta1 and Vta1's role in activating Vps4.

claim: Some archaeal species consist of only two ESCRT-III proteins.
source: Some archaeal species consist of only two ESCRT-III proteins, which must possess the minimal properties of ESCRT-III necessary for function (Caspi and Dekker, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In certain biological processes CHMP3 (mammalian Vps24) may play a minor role because the isoforms of CHMP2 (Vps2) may already possess the ability to form lateral interactions and recruit the AAA + ATPase Vps4.
source: These data provide an explanation for why in certain biological processes CHMP3 (mammalian Vps24) may play a minor role (such as in HIV budding), as the isoforms of CHMP2 (Vps2) may already possess the ability to form lateral interactions, and also an ability to recruit the AAA + ATPase Vps4.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data presented in the manuscript.
